#1401. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”

And that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

The Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

But the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2

Back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer

Predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

Boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

McGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

But Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

Marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

Four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

It’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

He had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the issue here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

Savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball launched to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

“You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

#1400. The Musiala case causes a huge outcry in Germany!

The controversy surrounding Jamal Musiala is far from falling on Bayern Munich. For several days, the Bavarian management’s comments on the future of the attacking midfielder and his imposing salary have sparked a wave of indignation in Germany. After Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, it is now Maik Franz who has stepped up to the plate. Guest of the show Doppelpass on Sport1the former defender did not mince his words to denounce the attitude of the Munich board, which he considers particularly inappropriate towards a player facing health problems. At the heart of this controversy, the statements of Rummenigge, who publicly questioned Musiala’s salary conditions in view of his physical difficulties and his level of performance.

An outing which provoked numerous reactions, notably from Maik Franz: “what the Bayern leaders are doing, and I’m not talking about Kompany and Eberl, who are behaving in an exemplary manner, but about MM. Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge, is pathetic and even, in my eyes, constitutes harassment. We can discuss a player’s performance. But it is not appropriate to talk publicly about an illness and the salary associated with it, at this level. We must not forget that Jamal tried everything to come back. He showed a lot of courage and transparency in discussing his diagnosis. For this to turn against him today is not acceptable. To be completely honest, we are no longer in “Mia san Mia”, but in “Mia san money”. Money takes precedence over people. And this must not happen.”.

The controversy even went beyond the borders of Bavarian management to affect the locker room. Michael Olise actually liked an Instagram post from Fabrizio Romano relaying the press release from FIFPRO, the international players’ union, which called on Bayern to respect Jamal Musiala. A particularly notable gesture from the French international, renowned for his discretion on social networks. This support takes on an additional dimension as Bayern wish to extend Olise’s contract, currently linked to the club until 2029. Maik Franz also underlined the risk that this affair could represent for decision-makers: “With Michael Olise, you may have the next best player in the world in your ranks. He too must extend and receive a big salary. But you keep in mind that if you got sick or injured and didn’t perform, you would be publicly thrown out to waste. Frankly, I don’t think they did themselves any favors.”.

FIFPRO also strongly criticized Bayern’s communication, saying contractual issues should be discussed privately with the player and his representatives. The union notably recalled that an injury or decline in form did not justify publicly calling into question salary conditions already agreed upon. While Musiala tries to regain his best level after a long period of absence, the Bavarian club finds itself under fire from critics. Between the declarations of its leaders, the exit of Maik Franz and the remarkable gesture of Olise, the file has become a real image issue for Bayern Munich…

#1399. Soule shines: 10 goal contributions in 17 matches

It wasn’t Hercules, but Matias Soulé who lit up the Parc des Princes.

The Argentine talent took just five minutes to become the star of yet another great European night: a decisive assist for Hermoso after dancing to the ball, skipping past opponents.

Gian Piero Gasperini expressed his satisfaction at seeing a player continually improving: “Besides being strong, he’s very positive, he’s receptive, and he wants to grow. He’s 23, and he’s in a period where he can grow, as he is doing. He’s more complete than before; today he’s played on the left, whereas until last year he was stuck on that pitch. He’s reaching extraordinary technical and physical maturity. I’m happy for him; in these last two months, he’s been doing something very positive.”

Matias Soulé shows no signs of slowing down his unstoppable growth. The Argentine winger has already been involved in 10 goals this season, one every 114 minutes: four goals and six assists in 17 appearances.

The Argentine talent’s performances this year are rising in proportion to the quality of his opponents: he has rarely been without a hand in big matches.

In fact, Soulé scored one goal and provided three assists in the Champions League matches against Real Madrid, Manchester United, and PSG.

In the league, he was instrumental with a goal that allowed Roma to a last-gasp 2-1 victory against Atalanta, adding to his assist for Hermoso that temporarily tied the game 1-1. On October 24, he lit up the Maradona stadium with a total performance from start to finish, further enhanced by the goal that sparked the comeback to secure a 3-3 draw at Napoli.

#1398. The story of Eric Cantona and his incredible impact on Man Utd

On May 17, 1997, Eric Cantona announced his retirement from football. He was only 30 years old, but his impact on Manchester United and on English football had been immeasurable.

“‘Ooh ahh, Cantona’? They won’t sing it here.”

That was one of the more extreme responses from a supporter outside Old Trafford (see video below) the day after Cantona stunned football – not for the first time and certainly not for the last – by signing for Manchester United.

As a 12-year-old red growing up in a Leeds United heartland, I certainly wasn’t sure how to process the breaking story late in the Calendar News bulletin at 6.25pm on Thursday, November 26, 1992.

Cantona had played a significant part in my misery up to that point, and his chant had provided the backing music for some merciless stick at school six months earlier when he helped Leeds deny my team their first Championship in 25 years. Yet here he was, switching sides.

Alex Ferguson did little to reassure his club’s supporters that there was method to the madness when he admitted Cantona only came into his mind “more or less” when Leeds called to enquire about Denis Irwin.

Cantona had only joined Leeds in January, signed for £900,000 by Howard Wilkinson from Nimes, and though the then-24-year-old made only six starts and another nine appearances off the bench in the second half of that 1991-92 season, his cameos helped Leeds beat Ferguson’s men to the title.

Cantona’s three goals came at home against teams in the lower half of the table, but he got the ball rolling against Luton and Wimbledon and broke Chelsea’s resistance with one of the goals of the season.

With Cantona, Leeds took 13 points from their final five games of the run-in, while Man Utd drew one and lost three on the spin against Nottingham Forest, West Ham and Liverpool to almost gift-wrap the final pre-Premier League title for their Yorkshire rivals.

Though Ferguson acknowledged in both autobiographies that Leeds were worthy champions, his side unquestionably blew it as his fear over the goals drying up became a reality.

Coincidence though it may be, when Leeds signed Cantona, Man Utd were averaging 2.9 goals per game over 26 matches. In the final 16-game run-in, that plummeted to one goal per game, while they were shut out six times.

Sixteen games into the following campaign, United were eighth and again averaging only a goal per game when a call took place which changed the face of English football.

“I remember that phone call clearly, as though it was yesterday,” Leeds’ former Managing director Bill Fotherby said in 2012.

“We agreed to pay Eric something like £500,000 if we kept him after the initial period of six months. It was an immense amount of money for Leeds, but we agreed to it because we had this recommendation from Michel Platini and we judged the most important thing was to get the player.

“We wanted to do whatever it took and deal with the rest afterwards. But there were difficulties almost immediately.

“Apart from Lee Chapman, no-one in the squad spoke fluent French, and for Howard, it was a bit of a nightmare. Although we had won the title, there was just no connection between the two and, in the end, he told me to try and find Eric another club.

“Howard Wilkinson was an absolute perfectionist. He wanted his players to be disciplined and adhere to a certain team pattern. Eric just didn’t fit it.

While Cantona might not have been suited to Leeds, he found his perfect match across the Pennines.

“If ever there was one player, anywhere in the word, that was made for Manchester United, it was Cantona,” said Ferguson later.

“He swaggered in, stuck his chest out, raised his head and surveyed everything as though he were asking: ‘I’m Cantona. How big are you? Are you big enough for me?’”

Ince, the self-styled Guvnor, said Cantona “took the responsibility away from us lot”, which was evident from the manner in which United attacked the second half of the season.

They doubled their goals per game over the remaining 26 matches, netting 50 times in 18 wins, losing only twice on their way to breaking a 26-year title drought. Famine was about to become feast.

Ferguson had been searching for a goalscorer, but in Cantona he found something rarer. The Frenchman notched nine goals over the remainder of the season, perhaps not a Shearer-esque strike-rate, but he offered 11 assists.

More than anything tangible, Cantona brought a swagger and a confidence which often strutted over the border to an arrogance that so inspired his team-mates and wowed fans at the now Stretford End-less Old Trafford.

With Bryan Robson’s powers waning, Cantona arrived at the perfect time. Countless team-mates have referenced how the Frenchman became the example to follow at The Cliff. They had a new leader.

Even Ferguson admits Cantona “opened my eyes to the indispensability of practice”.

With Cantona leading the line, United felt and often looked invincible. The burden of responsibility Ince referred to was gone, and they followed up the title in 1993 with their first-ever Double in 1994.

Cantona, with his collar up, was at the heart of all that the purists identified as good and bad about that 93-94 team. He scored 25 goals in all competitions and contributed 13 assists, earning himself the PFA Player of the Year award.

There was no sign of the temper United had been warned about until the Champions League trip to Galatasaray in November 1993 when Cantona received his first red card in a United shirt for insulting the referee, who he later accused of being “bought”.

As he and his team-mates descended down the steps towards the underground changing rooms, Cantona was slyly attacked by a baton and shield-wielding policeman, as was Robson when the skipper rushed to defend his team-mate.

“In the dressing room, Eric went crazy,” Roy Keane recalled in his autobiography. “While the rest of us just wanted to get out of there, Eric was determined to sort out the rogue cop who had been wielding his truncheon.

“Eric was a big, strong lad. He was serious. He insisted he was going to kill that f***er. It took the combined efforts of the manager, Brian Kidd and a few of the players to restrain him.”

Much like supporters, Cantona’s blood boiled at the thought of any perceived injustice, and that connection made it easy for United fans to not only forgive Eric’s misdemeanours but to revel in them.

Cantona simmered over later that season when he was banned for five games after red cards in successive draws at Swindon and Arsenal. But those incidents were merely child’s play compared to what was to come at Crystal Palace the following season.

The kung-fu kick on Matthew Simmons was the release of 48 minutes of frustration after Cantona had felt he had been kicked around Selhurst Park without any protection from Alan Wilkie.

Cantona questioned the referee at half-time while, according to Wilkie, Ferguson was more direct: “Why don’t you do your f*cking job!”

Three minutes after emerging from the tunnel for the second half, Cantona was being directed back towards it after dishing out his own form of justice to his shadow for the night, Richard Shaw.

Ferguson says he has “never been able to elicit an explanation from Eric” as to why he felt the need to react to Matthew Simmons that way. Unsurprisingly, it seems he did it because he felt like it.

“Millions of times people say these things, and then one day you don’t accept it,” Cantona said.

“Why? It’s not about words. It’s about how you feel at that moment. One day you react, but the words are exactly the same as those you have heard a million times, so it is impossible to say why you react.”

Cantona was subsequently suspended for nine months by the FA, and United went on to miss out on the title by a single point to Blackburn before losing the FA Cup final to Everton a week later.

To make matters worse, the FA threatened to extend Cantona’s suspension because he had been photographed taking part in a friendly against Rochdale that was nothing more than a behind-closed-doors kickabout of three thirds.

Cantona reacted by submitting a transfer request in early August.

Inter Milan, who were at Selhurst Park on that night in January to scout Cantona, would have been delighted to offer him a haven in Italy, but Ferguson travelled to Paris to convince his star player to stay put.

He later described that journey as “one of the more worthwhile acts I have performed in this stupid job of mine”.

Given the success that followed, that must rate as one of Ferguson’s greatest understatements. Another Double, this time with kids, and an additional Premier League title after that certainly justified his decision to smooth the path back for Cantona.

Cantona’s critics question his record, especially in European competition – though a goal every other game over six seasons and an assist for every three of his 185 appearances certainly stands up to scrutiny.

But Cantona’s contribution cannot be assessed by numbers.

United fans remember the moments. The good ones were incredible, and even the bad ones were great.

Important goals, like the volley at Newcastle to break Kevin Keegan’s heart or the retreating shot from the edge of the box to win the 1996 FA Cup final against Liverpool’s Spice Boys.

And great goals too, against Sunderland or an even better lob in a gale at Sheffield United.

Eric Cantona vs Sheffield United, 1995. pic.twitter.com/CukcNEykQm

— 90s Football (@90sfootball) June 27, 2020

In terms of technique, Cantona was the best Old Trafford had seen for some time, but with regard to charisma, he was perhaps the greatest ever.

Robson will always be revered – despite not being a United product, he was the Stretford End’s representative on the pitch. Work hard, play hard, tackle harder, Captain Marvel was easy to relate to, but Eric was an enigma as well as an icon.

Never misunderstood at Old Trafford but being barely understood by his public certainly added to the mercurial Frenchman’s charm.

Like many of us were told about Best, Law and Charlton, there is now a generation of supporters who were never lucky enough to experience Cantona first-hand, and no amount of YouTube highlights videos can make those poor souls feel what Eric made United fans feel in the 1990s.

#1396. IT'S A GAME CHANGER! Scotland to co-host Women's World Cup with England, Northern Ireland and Wales in 2035

Published: 13:05 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 23 November 2026

Scotland, England, Northern Ireland and Wales have been confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland (Hampden and Easter Road) and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

Joy for Spain after they defeated England in the 2023 Women's World Cup final

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the World Cup will take the nation's game to another level

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

For England this represents another chance to host a major women’s tournament, having hosted the European Championship in 2022 which the Lionesses won.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: 'The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

'Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep – and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.'

FIFA president Gianni Infantino announces the home nations as World Cup hosts

Scotland captain Caroline Weir added: 'The women’s game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

'We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.'

England forward Michelle Agyemang said it was 'incredibly special' and added: 'I’ve been lucky enough to know what it feels like to play for my country in a major tournament, and those are moments you dream about as a young girl playing football.

'The thought of another generation growing up knowing that the biggest stage in the game is coming to their home country is amazing. To have the chance to play in a home World Cup would be a dream, but even more exciting is thinking about all the girls watching who might see 2035 and believe they can be part of it one day.'

SFA chief Ian Maxwell says tournament will be 'most significant thing to happen to women's and girls' game in Scotland'

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be 'the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland'.

He said: 'The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.'

First Minister John Swinney said: 'This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

'The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls’ and women’s game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women’s football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

'Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.'

#1392. The best England kits of all time ranked & where to get them cheap on Black Friday

We’ve all got a World Cup 1990 England home shirt kicking around in a draw at home right? There’s a decent chance you’ve also got the red away shirt from the same period, popularised more recently by Jay from The Inbetweeners.

But what if your Three Lions fandom goes a little deeper? The 1982 World Cup squad of Kevin Keegan, Glenn Hoddle and Bryan Robson?

Perhaps you get your kicks from the disappointment of the 93-94 era? Well, the good news is Sports Direct’s range of Score Draw retro England shirts is in rude health, and discounted, in time for Black Friday – although for Football365 England Ladder fans there’s no Phil Neville 2007 shirt – yet (context: his final international appearance).

For the purposes of nostalgia then, here’s an 80s-born England fans top five from a range of 31.

Until the glory of World Cup 2018, I’d only ever seen England win one penalty shootout and it was thanks to the moustachioed ‘safe hands’ David Seaman.

Most people will go to Stuart Pearce’s redemption when they think of that shootout on the way to the Euro 96 semi-finals, but it was Arsenal star Seaman who saved Miguel Angel Nadal’s spot kick, and he did so in a memorable yellow patterned jersey.

Currently reduced by £10 to £51.99, it’s perfect for recreating a famous moment in the garden.

I’m too young to remember the Spain ’82 World Cup, but I watched endless England history and goals videos as a kid and the site of Robson scoring one of the fastest ever World Cup goals in footage that had the contrast turned up just a little too high is etched in my mind.

Perhaps setting me up for decades of disappointment, England romped Group 4 beating France, Czechoslovakia and Kuwait, sending the Three Lions into a second group stage where draws against Spain and West Germany weren’t enough.

England Spain 82 World Cup home and away shirts are on sale here.

Have England ever looked smarter than between 2004 and 2006? The answer is obviously no. And on the pitch, we’d been teased by Michael Owen but now we had Wayne Rooney, Steven Gerrard and David Beckham in his absolute pomp.

The smart collar, the tasteful red stripe across the shoulders. You could (and should) have worn this with a jacket and smart trousers. To a job interview. On your wedding day.

And the football. A spectacularly ill-tempered but crucial 0-0 draw in Turkey ahead of Euro 2004, not to mention Zinedine Zidane’s late show in the opening group game in Portugal and that infamous quarter-final defeat to the hosts.

Before the smart shirt. Before Jordan Pickford in a 2018 penalty shootout, before Jude Bellingham against Slovakia, there was 2002 World Cup David Beckham.

The shirt, a fairly bland white shirt brought to life by an unorthodox vertical thin red stripe up the left-hand side with the England badge overlaying it.

Think Germany 1 England 5, Beckham against Greece, Japan & South Korea, England 1 Argentina 0 and eventually, sadly, a back-pedalling David Seaman as Ronaldinho grinned away.

What a time to be alive, and a bargain with £15 off here.

This is a safe space? Possibly only a psychologist can unravel this, but the 93-94 home shirt was an absolute masterpiece for me. Possibly because I never owned it, and possibly because it was the first time I was properly engrossed in football, but despite not qualifying for World Cup 94 and stinking out Euro 92 either side of letting San Marino score a goal and ****** Ronald Koeman, I ached for this shirt and its extra little badge on the collar.

Why did it have an extra badge on the collar? It actually looks quite odd now.

Still, if you, like me yearn for a time when Wales were closer to qualifying for a tournament than England, this is the one for you.

Quite literally. In 92-93 England were still largely decked out in a version of the World Cup 1990 classics, but there was one right turn of a design choice in 1992 when a sky blue shirt with three huge lions running diagonally down from the left shoulder to the right arm pit was made available.

It was, criminally, only used twice in games against Czechoslovakia and Spain in March and September 1992, although the game against the Spanish in Santander marked Paul Ince’s international debut and Paul Merson’s first international goal came against the Czechs.

#1391. An XI of Man Utd fans who are better than the current Man Utd team

Manchester United‘s worldwide appeal, especially in the early 2000s, means there are plenty of current footballers who were fans of the club in their childhood.

Teams that are 19th in the Premier League don’t tend to have massive fanbases, but welcome to the contradiction that is modern Manchester United.

Here’s an XI of players who supported the club in their youth that are better than the current XI turning out for the club.

Considering some of the keepers United have had in recent years, how they could have used Courtois.

The Belgian keeper, who has become one of the very best, grew up a United fan due to Edwin van der Sar.

“I loved Edwin van der Sar and Casillas,” he told Rio Ferdinand. “So Casillas was because of his young age when he came into the goal at Madrid.

“At my age, I think I was like 12 or 11 at that time. Like I was just starting being goalkeeper. I really also blew my mind. Like, wow, he’s in Real Madrid.

“And I always followed those games. And then I followed always Manchester United for Edwin.”

He even revealed that he was close to joining United before they signed David de Gea.

Now at Lille, Thomas Meunier has long been pinning his colours to the United mast.

In 2017, he said: “I’m a big fan of Manchester United, which remains, in my eyes, the real reference in the world of football.”

And even recently, he said he would cycle to Manchester if given the opportunity.

“If they ever ask me, I’ll cycle there. But maybe it’s better this way. Suppose I play there and have a bad time. I wouldn’t want to hate Manchester United, because I love that club so much.

Akanji said he is “no longer” a United fan after he joined City but sorry Manuel, the internet has receipts.

He told German newspaper NZZ that he had been a United fan “since my childhood days.”

He quickly stopped talking about that since he signed for their city rivals, though.

Dier never outright said he was a United fan, but there are certainly signs.

Mainly, it was who he listed as his idols during an interview with the Players’ Tribune.

“I was a big fan of Roy Keane when I was younger, and then it was Nemanja Vidic (one of the reasons I like the number 15 is Vidic) and his defensive partner, Rio Ferdinand.”

He played a crucial part in City’s most successful ever period* but he was actually a United fan.

Stones has never outright said he grew up a United fan, maybe because the idea of Yorkshiremen doing so is a big no-no, but there is plenty of speculation online that he did indeed support the club.

Before he headed to Brighton, Caicedo named the two clubs in world football he would love to play for.

“In the short term: perform well and get Beerschot out of this plight. And in the long term? I am a fan of Manchester United and Real Madrid. It would be great to play there someday,” he told Gazet van Antwerpen.

A £100 million move to Chelsea has killed that dream for now but it would not be completely out of the question for him one day to be at Old Trafford.

Maddison’s support for United was spearheaded by David Beckham, who was playing for the Old Trafford side when Maddison was at the peak age when kids get drawn into football.

“In my early football days, I was a Manchester United fan and [Beckham] was at the forefront of that,” Maddison told talkSPORT.

“He was the guy on the back of my shirt, I went into the garden practising his free-kicks. The amount of times in school lessons I’d be watching David Beckham free-kicks on YouTube, it was silly really.”

How United could do with Beckham or Maddison now.

Palmer is just about the most famous Manchester United fan playing right now.

There is a picture often circulated online of Palmer as a boy wearing the 2010-11 home kit and in 2024, he confirmed he was a fan of the club as a child.

That fandom has him linked to United every transfer window.

Gibbs-White is another player to tell Rio Ferdinand that he was a United fan.

Speaking on the former United centre-back’s podcast, Gibbs-White picked out Rooney and Scholes as the players he most enjoyed watching.

“Growing up as a kid, I supported Man Utd. [Wayne] Rooney was always my favourite player. He was the key player in that squad. Another player I loved watching was Paul Scholes, he used to just pick the ball up and zing it everywhere.”

This one is a bit of rumour, but Nicky Butt claims that current Liverpool star Ngumoha was actually a United fan.

“I think he was at 13 or 14 or whatever age it was, he goes and looks around Man Utd – whether it be Old Trafford or Carrington,” Butt said on his podcast.

“He’s gone with his family to look around the football club, and then he’s gone to Liverpool. And he’s picked Liverpool, and he’s a Man Utd fan.

“He should not be allowed out of that building before he signed that contract. It would never have happened.”

Since signing for Liverpool, Ngumoha has clearly been told to never mention the United fandom thing.

Scoring in six consecutive matches has clearly made Evanilson confident he could fit in at a Big Six club and he has alerted United to the fact he is a big fan.

Evanilson told Globo Esporte: “So I joke around with Rayan. I think that, here in England, of the big clubs, United are the team I like the most. Rayan said the same thing. When I was a kid, I also used to watch United.

“When Cristiano Ronaldo played for United, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I’m here playing against them…

“It’s a dream, and I tell everyone this in interviews: it was a dream to play at that stadium, and scoring goals is even more important.

“So it’s a dream I’ve been fulfilling, scoring a goal against United because of how big the club is.”

#1388. Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday

The Istanbul Governor's Office said 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive

Reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’

Villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

To invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

#1387. The 8 highest-paid football pundits in 2026: Sky trio top the list

Punditry work is the lucrative alternative to management for retired ex-footballers and some earn more than a pretty penny for their time.

TV companies want ex-pros to front their coverage and for some audiences, watching the after-match debate has become as entertaining as watching the actual football.

As was the case when they were playing, the best ones get paid the big bucks but who are the biggest earners in football?

We’ve done our best to put together an accurate list but it is worth noting a couple of things. First off, the BBC’s Royal Charter means that they have to declare anyone who receives over £178k so anyone earning below that will not feature in this list.

Another important point to note is that the salaries of TNT pundits like Peter Crouch and Joe Cole are far more secretive than those at Sky.

But with those caveats in mind, here are the top earners in the UK.

Scott is the closest thing we have to Gary Lineker now that the former Match of the Day host has left in that player-turned-pundit-turned-presenter mould.

She has worked with the BBC since 2017, covering her first tournament at the 2018 World Cup, but was not picked as one of the hosts of Match of the Day.

Instead, she has branched out away from sport and also presents The One Show.

Some reports have Redknapp’s salary as high as £750k a year but that seems a little unrealistic.

Redknapp is on the B-tier of Sky Sports pundits, you will rarely see him on the Sunday 4:30pm game but he might be there for a Saturday 5:30.

He has been at Sky for a long time now having joined in 2006, he was even there in the Keys and Gray era, and is also a team captain on A League of Their Own.

Richards has fingers in many pies and so it is hard to nail down exactly what he earns.

What we do know is that he took home £205k from the BBC in their 2022 accounts but he was missing from the 2025/26 report so it must have dipped below £178k.

If we presume that it is still similar, Richards also appears on Sky and CBS, further inflating his pay packet.

To top it off, Richards is also one of the main faces on Gary Lineker’s Stick to Football podcast.

Alan Shearer took a 50k pay cut from 2025 to 2026 but still remains one of the best-paid pundits. With the departure of Gary Lineker, he became the highest-earning sports-related pundit in the BBC but has since lost that accolade.

He’s Match of the Day’s main pundit and was co-commentator for the BBC’s coverage of the World Cup Final this summer.

Rooney became a regular Match of the Day pundit in August 2025 after numerous attempts to stay in the managerial game failed.

Signing for the BBC, he reportedly put pen to paper on a two-year £800k deal.

He was one of the key pundits for the BBC’s World Cup coverage, most memorably calling the extended half-time break “crap”, and has defied doubters to actually be a decent pundit.

He’s currently on a hiatus from his BBC deal as he is being paid a reported £800k to appear on I’m a Celeb.

Would Wayne Rooney have worked in Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona?

“It’s your job,” he famously once said, and his job pays very well.

Keane’s exact contract details are not known but he is rumoured to be earning anywhere from £500k to £1m.

That comes from both his Sky work but also his regular appearances for ITV.

The main man for Monday Night Football ranks second in the best-paid pundits.

Carragher reportedly takes home £1m a year from his Sky deal which sees him feature on every big game as well as plenty of others.

Unlike his partner in crime Neville, Carragher does branch out away from Sky though and is part of CBS Sports’ coverage of the Champions League for US audiences.

Neville is the face of Sky Sports’ football coverage.

He reinvented the punditry role following his retirement in 2011 and if his early Monday Night Football performances were a little too high-pitched and awkward, he soon transformed into the perfect pundit.

These days, he has jumped the shark somewhat and is becoming increasingly depressed at Manchester United but his Stick to Football podcast has been backed by Global and Disney+.

For his Sky contract alone he is reported to be taking home £1.1m a year, making him the best-paid pundit in the UK.

#1386. The top 10 goalscorers worldwide in 2026: Harry Kane 3rd but outscored by forgotten England man

Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Al-Ahli and Dinamo Zagreb are among the clubs represented in the worldwide top 10 goalscorers of 2026.

There are some familiar superstar names alongside prolific forwards from leagues you might struggle to find on a map, with a few rather unexpected players outscoring some of Europe’s biggest stars. Lionel Messi has scored 30 goals for Inter Miami in 2026, but he just misses out on the top 10.

Here are the 10 most prolific club goalscorers in world football this calendar year, across all competitions.

A player you’ve (probably) never heard of. Get used to that.

Gambian midfielder Ousman Gai averages a goal every 60 minutes in 2026, which is the best ratio of any player in this top 10.

He finished as the top scorer in the Philippines Football League last season, firing Manila Digger to the league title, a return that earned him a move to Cambodian outfit Visakha in the summer.

We all love a journeyman Brazilian playing in a far-flung league, don’t we?

Chigor is a classic of the genre, having developed his skills in the Red Bull system and gone on to play for the energy brand’s Bragantino club.

After representing eight clubs in Brazil, the forward moved to Thailand in 2024 and is currently leading the line for Malaysian outfit Selangor. He’s scored 34 goals in just 33 appearances for the club in 2026.

The most prolific goalscorer you’ve never heard of.

After some short-lived loans in South Korea and Portugal as a youngster, Bergson spent most of his twenties moving around Brazil without making much of an impression.

But he found a settled home at Malaysian giants Johor Darul Ta’zim since signing for the club as a 30-year-old back in 2021. He’s notched an insane tally of 203 goals in 200 appearances for the club and shows little sign of slowing down, with 34 in 2026 so far.

The former Brazil youth international was recently cleared by FIFA to switch his allegiance to represent Malaysia, and he’s already scored a hat-trick for the national team against Singapore.

Not that one. The former Barcelona and Liverpool man has scored a few for Inter Miami this year, but he’s slowing down considerably in his twilight years.

No, this is the Colombian one, once of Watford, who is now taking Viktor Gyokeres’ place in scoring for fun at Manchester United.

He’d be even higher if he’d converted both of the penalties he took against Manchester United in midweek.

You remember him. The World Cup cult hero and surprise 2026 Ballon d’Or nominee won the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot last season, having notched five more goals than Al-Nassr title-winner Cristiano Ronaldo.

Quinoses has scored 36 goals for Al-Qadsiah this calendar year, although he’s not quite the top Saudi-based goalscorer of 2026. It’s not Ronaldo – can you guess who?

Keep this up and you wonder if a European club might take a punt on the 29-year-old Mexico international.

The 23-year-old Puerto Rican has recently moved to DS Edusoccer after an outrageous goalscoring return for Academia Quintana.

Seven(!) goals in one game help out quite a bit here. He scored them in an 18-1(!!) victory over FC Mayaguez.

The oldest player in this top 10, Zampedri earned his first two senior Chile caps last year after blossoming in his mid-thirties with Universidad Catolica.

He was born and raised in Argentina but switched international allegiance after thriving in the country’s top flight over the past few years.

The 38-year-old has fired Universidad Catolica to two Primera Division de Chile league titles and won the Golden Boot in each of the last six seasons, with a seventh pretty much in the bag for 2026.

You knew he’d be here. Comfortably the top goalscorer when it comes to major European football in 2026. And he’s even further ahead if you count his bounty of goals for England.

Kane isn’t the England international with the most club goals in 2026, somehow.

Toney was pipped to the Saudi Pro League by Quinoses last season, but he’s the early frontrunner this season with 14 goals from just 10 appearances this season.

That takes his overall tally to 44 goals this calendar year for Al Ahli. Every chance he tops this list when all is said and done come New Year’s Day.

It’ll be interesting to see whether he has another Premier League stint in him. Given his goalscoring output, you’d take a punt, wouldn’t you? Whether he’d be willing to take a wage cut is another question – but maybe when his current deal expires in 2028.

We expected the leader to be a total unknown playing in the middle of nowhere, but Beljo is actually somewhat established.

The 24-year-old is a full Croatia international with experience playing in a top European league, although he failed to pull up any trees in the Bundesliga with Augsburg.

He’s been outrageously prolific since returning to Croatia with the perennial champions Dinamo Zagreb in 2025. He notched 38 goals in all competitions in his debut season and appears set to better that tally in year two.

Beljo recently scored against Sunderland in the Europa League. Keep this up, and another opportunity at a higher level will surely come calling. Leeds United are among a host of clubs who have been linked.
