#1330. Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s new biology skills wow scientists

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0)

Earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology company called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed new proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

The research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” says Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

But some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

The release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing new proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

In other experiments, the OpenAI team showed that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

Jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03836-z

#1329. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

#1328. Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1327. Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

“My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, says Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, said Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts currently on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration

Ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang said.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty

#1326. Alejandro Garnacho's nightmare Aston Villa loan continues: Struggling star is left at home as Unai Emery picks TWO goalkeepers on bench for Galatasaray defeat before sending warning to ex-Man United winger

Published: 17:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 24 November 2026

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery said: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'

Daily Mail Sport has reported regularly this season that Garnacho may not see out his loan spell and now that looks increasingly likely to be the case.

There is not thought to be a break clause in the loan but if Chelsea and Villa agreed to cancel it, that would allow Garnacho to go elsewhere in January.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday

Villa boss Unai Emery chose to include two goalkeepers on his bench instead of picking of him

Villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

He said: 'I am not blaming the referee but he was unfair with us by adding only five minutes. After they scored it was impossible to play.'

#1325. Bruno Fernandes opens door to Sporting return amid doubts over Man United future as captain insists 'now is not the time' to discuss new contract

Published: 17:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:54 EST, 24 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has left the door open for a return to Sporting Lisbon amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Manchester United.

Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.

The United captain has become equally popular at Old Trafford, but returned to Lisbon on Tuesday night with a question mark hanging over his next move after talks over a new contract stalled.

Fernandes’ current deal is due to run out at the end of June – and he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January 1 – although United are expected to trigger an automatic 12-month extension to prevent him from leaving as a free agent in the summer.

Asked if he would consider a move back to the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where United meet Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Fernandes said: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.

‘Sporting was the first club that believed in my potential. I’ve always felt here from the fans – regardless of what may have happened – all the love and kindness from them, and that was essential to make me grow as a player.’

Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a new contract to extend his stay at Man United

On his future at Old Trafford, Fernandes insisted that he wants to focus on turning United’s season around after they slipped into the relegation zone and replaced head coach Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.

‘Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games, and then we can talk about a contract. Now is not the moment.’

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

#1322. One Change For Blues At Brentford

Jake O'Brien comes back into the starting XI as the only change for Everton's Premier League clash away to Brentford (8pm GMT).

With the Blues bidding to build on their three-game winning streak ahead of the recent international break, manager David Moyes – on his record-breaking 593rd game in charge of the Club – names the same line-up that triumphed 1-0 at Newcastle United on 2 November.

That sees O'Brien start at right-back, with Merlin Röhl moving forward to right wing in place of Tyler Dibling. The rest of Everton's backline is made up of keeper Jordan Pickford, central defenders James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite, and Vitalii Mykolenko.

The Toffees' central midfield three is once again formed of James Garner, Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, with Tyrique George on the left flank and in-form striker Thierno Barry up top.

The Blues' bench includes former Brentford captain Christian Nørgaard and Jack Grealish.

Everton XI: Pickford, O'Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko, Garner, Armstrong, Dewsbury-Hall, Röhl, George, Barry.

Subs: Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, Dibling, Johnson, Nørgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney.

#1321. Ten-Man Blues Undone At Brentford

Everton’s return to Premier League action proved a forgettable one as a 17-minute first-half spell ultimately condemned them to a 4-0 defeat at Brentford.

Looking to extend their three-match unbeaten run built before the recent international break, the Blues struggled to get going at the Gtech Stadium – before rotten luck left them with a mountain to climb.

On 23 minutes, Keane Lewis-Potter’s run into the area was picked out by Jaidon Anthony as his finish took a horrible deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite to beat Jordan Pickford.

Worse misfortune struck Everton two minutes later as Lewis-Potter’s shot was blocked by James Tarkowski, fell straight back into the path of the same Brentford player whose rebound was destined to be kept out again, only to hit Thierno Barry and wrong-foot Pickford.

The Toffees’ hopes of mounting a comeback were then all but ended five minutes before the interval when Tarkowski was penalised for a sliding tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Initially slow to award the free-kick, referee Craig Pawson eventually showed the Blues captain a yellow card – only to be called over by VAR and soon change his decision to red for violent conduct.

Left to battle on with 10 men, Everton had a sniff of a comeback with seconds left of the first half when fine work from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ended with the No.8 chipping in a cross that Barry did well to nod into the bottom right-hand corner, only for keeper Caoimhin Kelleher to somehow claw the ball away.

Jack Grealish came on for the start of the second half and soon made an impact with a teasing centre across the six-yard box that just evaded Barry.

But any hopes of an unlikely fightback were ended on 67 minutes as Vitaly Janelt fired a 25-yard strike into the top right-hand corner.

And a miserable night was summed up in the dying moments when Damsgaard's corner found its way to substitute Fabio Carvalho to tap over the line from a yard out.

#1320. Florian Wirtz opens up on chats with ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp and thanks Andoni Iraola after starring role in Man United thrashing

Published: 18:12 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:24 EST, 24 November 2026

Florian Wirtz has thanked Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola for sparking his resurgence and insists he never stopped believing in himself.

The German arrived with a big reputation when he completed a £116million move from Bayer Leverkusen but has been a constant punchbag for critics after failing to reach the heights that saw him win the Bundesliga title as the league’s star man.

Wirtz, though, has been much improved this year and put in his best performance for the Reds on Sunday in the 4-0 thumping of Manchester United And he insists Iraola – and old Anfield boss Jurgen Klopp – are the reason.

‘I am really enjoying playing under him,’ said Wirtz on Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer. ‘He is a really good coach. He has shown that his whole career as a manager.

‘He is bringing me back to the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football.

‘I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me. I am really happy with that.’

Florian Wirtz has opened up on talking to ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp after finally hitting form for Liverpool

Wirtz won man of the match in Liverpool's 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United on Sunday

Wirtz has also had the added influence of Klopp, now Germany boss, in recent months. He said: ‘We always speak about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He is the coach who stayed here the most of his career.

‘He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to get successful over here because he has shown how it is done.

'He knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here, he can give me some good advice.’

Wirtz added: ‘It's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself.

‘I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities and I know them now. Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I'm just enjoying the moment and really happy at the moment that it's going well. I'm happy with myself.’

Meanwhile, Cody Gakpo will miss the Merseyside derby with a calf problem and fellow Dutchman Ryan Gravenberch is also in a race against time to be fit for the trip to Everton due to a fascia issue. Neither have travelled to Belgium for Liverpool’s clash against Club Brugge.
